results.evidence: validate.py now yields (founder_time_h,), RULE_FINITE when the value is not math.isfinite. The new test writes raw JSON with the bare Infinity literal and runs the real prospects-import. It asserts the output contains 'rejected record 1: founder_time_h:' and that every table has 0 rows, so no lead is written. `uv run --offline pytest -q tests/test_prospects_finite_founder_time.py` gave 8 passed. The Infinity case is covered, as are NaN, -Infinity and CSV inf.

validate.py adds a finite check on founder_time_h that yields a failure on field founder_time_h. The new tests feed a JSON record with the bare NaN literal and a CSV row with cell 'inf' through the import path. Each is rejected with 'rejected record 1: founder_time_h:' and nothing is written to the db. All 8 tests pass.

test_a_finite_founder_time_still_imports writes a JSON record with founder_time_h 1.5, runs the real import, asserts exit OK and that SELECT founder_time_h FROM leads returns [1.5]. The test file passed (8 passed). The new finite check in validate.py only yields a failure when math.isfinite is false, so 1.5 is not rejected.
